about: I'm a researcher and software engineer who enjoys turning challenging problems into useful, dependable systems.
I'm pursuing a PhD through the UKRI SAINTS Centre for Doctoral Training at the University of York, investigating safety, uncertainty and risk-aware autonomous systems.
Before that, I graduated from York with First Class Honours in Computer Science. My undergraduate research on deep learning for underwater object detection led to two peer-reviewed publications.

Alongside research, I work at Dashing Distribution Software on architecture and full-stack delivery for complex business workflows: enterprise platforms, integrations, automation and practical AI applications.
I care about the details of how systems work, but even more about whether they solve the right problems and behave reliably when it matters.
motivation: I grew up in Nepal, where landslides and extreme weather are part of life. Seeing their effects first hand is a large part of why I care about technology that makes disaster assessment safer and more effective, and why my research focuses on autonomous systems that know when they are unsure.
